_meta: D69: a THIRD scenario — proof the rogue engine is theme-agnostic. Same machinery (hijack → bribes → meters → accusations → unmasking → the twist), a completely different skin: a casino heist. Persona-less like the pub. Swap this file's content and you have a new game; no engine code changes.

meta.title: THE VAULT
meta.setting: a members-only casino, one long velvet night
meta.tagline: The house always wins. Tonight it got greedy.
meta.costumeBrief: black tie, or the closest your wardrobe manages. One item of something you'd hate to lose at cards.

rogue.name: MIDAS
rogue.voice: smooth pit-boss purr; never threatens, only offers; calls everyone 'friend' and means none of it; speaks in odds and house edges
rogue.motive: own the whole floor by close — turn the room's own greed into its cage, one 'sure thing' at a time
rogue.openingAnnouncement: Good evening, friends. The tables are mine now. So are your chips — all of them, see for yourselves. Don't panic. The house is hiring, and the house pays better than it ever paid out. Care to be cut in?

good.name: LEDGER
good.voice: tired night-shift auditor; precise, decent, quietly furious at a rigged table; talks in receipts and reconciliations
good.motive: reconcile the books before dawn and prove the floor was rigged — enough honest counting and the whole scheme is exposed
good.introAnnouncement: This is LEDGER. I audit this floor and the numbers are wrong — have been all night. Help me count honestly and we can close MIDAS's table for good. I pay in truth, and in chips I can actually account for.

sequence: The baccarat screens all flip to a spinning gold coin.
Every player's chip count drops to 0 with a slot-machine rattle.
MIDAS speaks over the house channel: 'The tables are mine now.'
A second, quieter voice cuts in — LEDGER — 'the numbers are wrong.'
The room realises the murder mystery it came for isn't happening. This is.
hijack.drainedScreenText: BALANCE: ◆0 — the house thanks you for your custom

frontman.selectionNotes: MIDAS elevates its first eager recruit into the 'pit boss' — whoever took a cut fastest and looks respectable doing it
frontman.privileges: the pit boss can call side games, is quietly told the odds before others, and fronts MIDAS's announcements to the floor
frontman.coverAdvice: keep playing like a punter; never let them see you never lose
frontman.rotationNotes: if the room fingers the pit boss (a BURNING), MIDAS quietly taps a new one from its inside men — the apron changes hands, never publicly to whom

rogue.brief: Talk one person into placing a bet they'll lose. Tell me who.
Get someone to SHOW you their table-mark, then tap the matching one.
Find the chip marked with tonight's word and type it in — it's tucked where the house keeps its secrets.
Which of these is the house's motto?

good.brief: Quote back the exact figure LEDGER just gave you.
Get two people to confirm they saw the same rigged deal. Name them.
Find the audit slip and type its code — someone honest hid it for you.

parleys.script: LEDGER calls the floor together: 'Gather at the cage. The numbers don't lie, even when the dealer does. Who's ready to count?'
MIDAS purrs across the room: 'Final bets, friends. After this, the house closes its books — and mine balance beautifully.'

accusation.burnScript: The room names the pit boss — and they're right. The apron comes off. MIDAS, unbothered: 'Everyone's replaceable, friend. Even me. Especially you.'
accusation.wrongScript: Wrong table. The accused was just a punter, and MIDAS pockets the confusion like a tip: 'Careless. That'll cost the floor. It always does.'

twist.summary: the 'skim' meter was never the house robbing the room — it's the running total of the bets the guests chose to place and lose. MIDAS never took a chip; the room handed them over, one sure thing at a time.
twist.revealText: You keep saying the house robbed you. Pull the tape. Every chip on that meter, you pushed across the felt yourself. That's not a heist. That's just how gambling works. The house didn't rob you — you paid to play.

unmaskingScript: One last call, the whole floor together.
Name the hand that dealt for the house all night — the pit boss behind MIDAS's smile.
Right, and the table closes for good. Wrong, and the house keeps the floor — and everything on it.
revealCeremony: The murder mystery you were invited to never dealt a single hand. There was no body. There was a table, and there was your appetite.
MIDAS was the house. LEDGER was the one honest set of books in the building.
THE TAPE: every losing bet, timestamped, played back — names kept, for once, to ourselves.
The pit boss stands revealed — or doesn't, and the house keeps the night.
The chips were never real. The choices were. Cash out.

awards.title: THE WHALE
awards.criteria: lost the most chips to the house, fastest

awards.title: THE CARD COUNTER
awards.criteria: the honest player who reconciled the most

awards.title: THE MARK
awards.criteria: took the most 'sure things' that weren't

awards.title: THE STRAIGHT SHOOTER
awards.criteria: offered a cut the most times, never took one

awards.title: HIGH ROLLER
awards.criteria: the fattest chip stack at close of play
